topic: Stock Purchases and Sales: Long and Short
source_evidence: The investor later closes out the position by returning the borrowed security to the stock lender, typically by purchasing securities on the open market.
answer: In a short sale, an investor sells a stock they do not own, usually by borrowing it. To close the position later, they typically buy the stock in the market and return it to the lender. If the price has fallen, buying it back at the lower price can result in a profit; if the price has risen, buying it back at the higher price results in a loss. Short sellers may also have to pay fees or interest on the stock loan, and are responsible for paying any dividend on the borrowed stock.
